title: What Was the USA Like in 1776?
speaker: Tom Wilkinson

keywords.def: a person who lives in a colony, especially one that is controlled by another country
the state of being free from the control or rule of another country, government, or authority
a person who lives under the rule of a king, queen, or other monarch and owes loyalty to them
a major and often sudden change in a country’s political system, usually involving the removal of an existing government
a person who is chosen to speak, act, or make decisions on behalf of a group of people
a person chosen to represent a group, organisation, or region at an official meeting or conference
the freedom to think, act, and live as you choose without unnecessary restrictions from authority.

sentences.en: When I think of the USA, I picture New York’s skyscrapers, Hollywood movies, and Silicon Valley technology companies.
sentences.zh: 当我想到美国时，我的脑海中会浮现出纽约的摩天大楼、好莱坞电影以及硅谷的技术公司。

sentences.en: I think of the world’s largest economy, and the most powerful country, with a population of more the 340 million people.
sentences.zh: 我想到了世界最大经济体、最具权势的国家，拥有超过三亿四千万的人口。

sentences.en: But what was the USA like when it was first founded?
sentences.zh: 但最初建国时的美国是什么样子的呢？

sentences.en: This year, the US is celebrating the 250 th anniversary since it declared independence from the British Empire.
sentences.zh: 今年，美国正在庆祝其宣布脱离大英帝国独立二百五十周年。

sentences.en: I thought it would be interesting to spend this episode considering what the USA was like two hundred and fifty years ago.
sentences.zh: 我觉得花这一期节目来思考二百五十年前的美国是怎样的会很有趣。

sentences.en: Back when it was thirteen separate colonies, that were not united at all, and before there was a concept of being an “American” or being a citizen of the USA.
sentences.zh: 回到当时它还是十三个各自独立的殖民地、完全没有联合起来的时候，并且在“美国人”或美国公民的概念出现之前。

sentences.en: I’m going to talk about the original colonies, the declaration of independence, the revolutionary war, and how the USA developed.
sentences.zh: 我将谈谈最初的殖民地、独立宣言、独立战争，以及美国是如何发展起来的。

sentences.en: At the same time, we will be practicing our English listening comprehension and learning some new vocabulary!
sentences.zh: 同时，我们也将练习英语听力理解并学习一些新词汇！

sentences.en: Before 1776, the United States did not exist.
sentences.zh: 在1776年之前，美国并不存在。

sentences.en: Technically, there were no states to be united.
sentences.zh: 严格来说，当时并没有可以被联合的州。

sentences.en: Instead, there were thirteen separate British colonies spread along the Atlantic Coast of North America.
sentences.zh: 取而代之的是分布在北美洲大西洋沿岸的十三个各自独立的英国殖民地。

sentences.en: A colony is a territory controlled and governed by another country.
sentences.zh: 殖民地是指被另一个国家控制和管辖的领土。

sentences.en: In this case, the colonies were under the authority, under the rule, of Britain and the British Crown.
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，这些殖民地受制于英国和英国王室的权威与统治。

sentences.en: Most of these colonies had been established during the 1600s, maybe the early 1700s.
sentences.zh: 这些殖民地大多是在17世纪或18世纪初建立的。

sentences.en: Some had been founded by companies hoping to make money.
sentences.zh: 有些是由希望赚钱的公司建立的。

sentences.en: Some others were created by religious groups seeking freedom from persecution.
sentences.zh: 另一些则是由寻求摆脱宗教迫害的宗教团体创建的。

sentences.en: The first permanent English colony was Jamestown, Virginia, founded in 1607.
sentences.zh: 第一个永久性的英国殖民地是1607年建立的弗吉尼亚州詹姆斯敦。

sentences.en: The initial settlers really struggled with disease, food shortages, and they were often in conflict with the local indigenous people.
sentences.zh: 最初的定居者确实在疾病和食物短缺中挣扎，并且他们经常与当地土著居民发生冲突。

sentences.en: But over time, Virginia became prosperous.
sentences.zh: 但随着时间推移，弗吉尼亚变得繁荣起来。

sentences.en: It became successful, especially through the production of tobacco.
sentences.zh: 它取得了成功，尤其是通过烟草的生产。

sentences.en: A few years later in 1620, another famous group of settlers arrived aboard a boat called the Mayflower.
sentences.zh: 几年后的1620年，另一群著名的定居者乘坐一艘名为“五月花”号的船抵达。

sentences.en: They established Plymouth Colony in present-day Massachusetts.
sentences.zh: 他们在如今的马萨诸塞州建立了普利茅斯殖民地。

sentences.en: These settlers are often called the Pilgrims.
sentences.zh: 这些定居者通常被称为清教徒。

sentences.en: They were a strict type of Protestant Christian, and they were seeking the freedom to practice their religion according to their own beliefs.
sentences.zh: 他们是新教基督徒中比较严厉的一个派别，寻求按照自己的信仰来实践宗教的自由。

sentences.en: Over the following century, more colonies appeared along the coast.
sentences.zh: 在接下来的一个世纪里，更多的殖民地沿着海岸出现。

sentences.en: By the mid-1700s, Britain possessed thirteen colonies down the coast of the modern USA.
sentences.zh: 到18世纪中期，英国在现代美国海岸线沿线拥有了十三个殖民地。

sentences.en: There were actually more colonies up in modern-day Canada and in the Caribbean as well.
sentences.zh: 实际上，在现代加拿大和加勒比地区也有更多的殖民地。

sentences.en: These colonies were not united. They were separate.​ Usually, they are grouped into three different categories.
sentences.zh: 这些殖民地并不是联合在一起的。它们是独立的。通常，它们被分为三个不同的类别。

sentences.en: The Northern Colonies, often known as New England, included New Hampshire, Massachusetts Bay, Rhode Island, and Connecticut.
sentences.zh: 北部殖民地通常被称为新英格兰，包括新罕布什尔、马萨诸塞湾、罗德岛和康涅狄格。

sentences.en: They developed around fishing and shipping and trade.
sentences.zh: 它们围绕着渔业、航运和贸易发展起来。

sentences.en: The towns there were relatively dense, and the education levels, the literacy rates, were a bit higher than other parts of British North America.
sentences.zh: 那里的城镇相对密集，教育水平和识字率比英属北美的其他地区要高一些。

sentences.en: The Middle Colonies included New York, New Jersey, Delaware, and Pennsylvania.
sentences.zh: 中部殖民地包括纽约、新泽西、特拉华和宾夕法尼亚。

sentences.en: This was the most diverse part of British North America.
sentences.zh: 这是英属北美最多元化的地区。

sentences.en: People from England, Germany, the Netherlands, Sweden, and many other places settled there.
sentences.zh: 来自英国、德国、荷兰、瑞典和许多其他地方的人们在那里定居。

sentences.en: In fact, New York and I think parts of New Jersey used to be under Dutch control, and famously, the island of Manhattan used to be called New Amsterdam.
sentences.zh: 事实上，纽约而且我想新泽西的一部分以前是受荷兰控制的，并且众所周知，曼哈顿岛以前被称为新阿姆斯特丹。

sentences.en: The Southern Colonies included Maryland, Virginia, North Carolina, South Carolina, and Georgia.
sentences.zh: 南部殖民地包括马里兰、弗吉尼亚、北卡罗来纳、南卡罗来纳和佐治亚。

sentences.en: The South developed a very different economy.
sentences.zh: 南方发展出了非常不同的经济。

sentences.en: They had large plantations which produced crops such as tobacco, rice, and indigo.
sentences.zh: 他们拥有生产烟草、水稻和靛蓝等农作物的大型种植园。

sentences.en: These were very valuable things. These plantations relied heavily on African slaves.
sentences.zh: 这些是非常有价值的东西。这些种植园严重依赖非洲奴隶。

sentences.en: What this means, the fact that there were different colonies, is that the people there lived completely different lives.
sentences.zh: 这意味着，由于存在不同的殖民地，那里的人们过着截然不同的生活。

sentences.en: There was not really much connecting a merchant in Boston with a plantation owner in Georgia.
sentences.zh: 波士顿的商人和佐治亚的种植园主之间并没有太多的联系。

sentences.en: Actually, the thing that connected these people would be Britain.
sentences.zh: 事实上，连接这些人的纽带会是英国。

sentences.en: They probably didn’t see themselves as Americans, like people in the USA do today anyway.
sentences.zh: 无论如何，他们可能并不把自己看作美国人，就像今天的美国人那样。

sentences.en: They would’ve seen themselves as British subjects.
sentences.zh: 他们会把自己视为英国臣民。

sentences.en: They spoke English, they traded with Britain, and they lived under British laws.
sentences.zh: 他们说英语，与英国进行贸易，并生活在英国法律之下。

sentences.en: It was probably more common for someone from Massachusetts to visit Britain than it was to visit the south of the British colonies.
sentences.zh: 对马萨诸塞州的人来说，去英国访问可能比去英国殖民地的南部更常见。

sentences.en: But as the colonies grew wealthier, questions started to appear around who should govern them, and what rights British subjects possessed abroad.
sentences.zh: 但随着殖民地变得越来越富有，开始出现关于谁应该统治它们以及英国臣民在海外拥有什么权利的疑问。

sentences.en: One of the most important things to understand about the American Revolution is that the conflict did not necessarily begin because people from British North America saw themselves as a separate people who wanted their own country.
sentences.zh: 关于美国革命，最需要理解的重要事情之一是，这场冲突的爆发并不一定是因为英属北美的人们觉得自己是一个想要自己国家的独立群体。

sentences.en: Many of the colonists actually considered themselves to be British.
sentences.zh: 许多殖民地居民实际上认为自己是英国人。

sentences.en: A lot of them were born in Britain, and they argued that they deserved the same rights as people living in Britain.
sentences.zh: 他们当中有很多人出生在英国，他们认为自己理应享有与生活在英国的人同样的权利。

sentences.en: Let me give you some more background information.
sentences.zh: 让我给你们提供更多背景信息。

sentences.en: From 1756 to 1773, Britain fought in the Seven Years’ War.
sentences.zh: 从1756年到1773年，英国参与了七年战争。

sentences.en: This war was fought across Europe, North America, the Caribbean, Africa, and Asia.
sentences.zh: 这场战争在欧洲、北美、加勒比地区、非洲和亚洲全面爆发。

sentences.en: Numerous different countries were involved, but at its simplest, it was basically Britain and Prussia fighting against France and Austria.
sentences.zh: 许多不同的国家卷入其中，但最简单地说，它基本上是英国和普鲁士与法国和奥地利交战。

sentences.en: Some historians describe this as the first true world war.
sentences.zh: 一些历史学家将此描述为第一次真正意义上的世界大战。

sentences.en: Britain won the war. They gained a lot of new territories from winning, and they became an even stronger global empire.
sentences.zh: 英国赢得了战争。他们通过获胜获得了大量新领土，并成为了一个更加强大的全球帝国。

sentences.en: But the war was really expensive. Britain was now in a lot of debt.
sentences.zh: 但战争成本极高。英国现在背负了大量债务。

sentences.en: They’d had to borrow money to fund their war effort.
sentences.zh: 他们不得不借钱来资助他们的战争努力。

sentences.en: British politicians believed it was reasonable for the American colonies to pay more taxes to fund things like defense.
sentences.zh: 英国政治家认为，美洲殖民地支付更多税款来资助防御等事务是合理的。

sentences.en: In 1765, Britain introduced the Stamp Act, which required some printed materials, like newspapers or legal documents, to be taxed.
sentences.zh: 1765年，英国颁布了《印花税法》，要求对报纸或法律文件等一些印刷材料征税。

sentences.en: And then over the next few years, they kept introducing more taxes in North America.
sentences.zh: 随后在接下来的几年里，他们不断在北美推出更多税收。

sentences.en: This angered the colonists. They argued that they were being taxed by a parliament, the parliament in London, in which they had no elected representatives.
sentences.zh: 这激怒了殖民地居民。他们辩称，他们被一个连一个民选代表都没有的议会——伦敦的议会——征税。

sentences.en: There was no Member of Parliament for North America.
sentences.zh: 北美没有国会议员。

sentences.en: You’ve probably heard the famous slogan, ‘ No taxation without representation ‘.
sentences.zh: 你可能听过那句著名的口号，“无代表不纳税”。

sentences.en: This is the story that’s often told when talking about the American Revolution.
sentences.zh: 这是在谈论美国革命时经常被讲述的故事。

sentences.en: One of the most famous incidents happened in 1773.
sentences.zh: 最著名的事件之一发生在1773年。

sentences.en: A group of colonists boarded a British ship in Boston Harbor and dumped hundreds of chests of tea into the water.
sentences.zh: 一群殖民地居民登上波士顿港的一艘英国船只，把数百箱茶倒进了水里。

sentences.en: They did this to protest a tax on tea. The event became known as the Boston Tea Party.
sentences.zh: 他们这样做是为了抗议对茶征税。这一事件后来被称为波士顿倾茶事件。

sentences.en: This was also one of the moments when the thirteen colonies started to work together and cooperate for the first time.​ The colonists were also debating some really big political questions.
sentences.zh: 这也是十三块殖民地开始第一次共同协作的时刻之一。殖民地居民还在辩论一些非常重大的政治问题。

sentences.en: Who should hold power? Where does government get its authority from?
sentences.zh: 谁应该掌握权力？政府的权力从何而来？

sentences.en: Do people have rights that governments cannot take away?
sentences.zh: 人们是否拥有政府不能剥夺的权利？

sentences.en: These were questions that were being discussed across Europe during a period known as the Enlightenment.
sentences.zh: 这些是在被称为启蒙运动的时期全欧洲都在讨论的问题。

sentences.en: The Enlightenment was an intellectual movement that encouraged people to use reason and evidence to understand the world.
sentences.zh: 启蒙运动是一场鼓励人们运用理性和证据来理解世界的思想运动。

sentences.en: Enlightenment thinkers argued that societies should be organized according to principles, rational principles, not just accepting traditions.
sentences.zh: 启蒙思想家认为，社会的组织应该根据原则、理性原则，而不仅仅是接受传统。

sentences.en: One of the most influential thinkers for the American colonists was John Locke.
sentences.zh: 对美洲殖民地居民最具影响力的思想家之一是约翰·洛克。

sentences.en: Locke argued that people possess natural rights.
sentences.zh: 洛克认为人类拥有自然权利。

sentences.en: They have rights just for being human. These rights include life, liberty, and property.
sentences.zh: 他们仅仅因为是人类就拥有权利。这些权利包括生命、自由和财产。

sentences.en: According to Locke, the government exists to protect people’s rights.
sentences.zh: 根据洛克的观点，政府的存在是为了保护人们的权利。

sentences.en: Governments get their power from the people in order to protect the people’s rights.
sentences.zh: 政府从人民那里获得权力，以便保护人民的权利。

sentences.en: Locke also argued that citizens have the right to resist a government or replace their government if they were no longer protecting people’s rights, or if they were violating people’s rights.
sentences.zh: 洛克还认为，如果政府不再保护人们的权利，或者如果它们在侵犯人们的权利，公民有权抵抗或更换他们的政府。

sentences.en: This was quite different from the European conception of government.
sentences.zh: 这与欧洲对政府的概念截然不同。

sentences.en: For centuries, a lot of Europe had been ruled by monarchs, kings, queens, emperors, princes, other kinds of royalty.
sentences.zh: 几个世纪以来，欧洲的许多地方一直由君主、国王、女王、皇帝、亲王和其他种类的皇室统治。

sentences.en: They claimed power due to their birth or due to tradition.
sentences.zh: 他们声称权力来自于他们的出生或传统。

sentences.en: They did not claim power because they were going to protect people’s rights.
sentences.zh: 他们声称权力不是因为他们要保护人们的权利。

sentences.en: They did not get power from the people. They got it from tradition.
sentences.zh: 他们不是从人民那里获得权力的。他们从传统中获得权力。

sentences.en: Kings ruled because they were kings. Why is that person king?
sentences.zh: 国王统治是因为他们是国王。为什么那个人是国王？

sentences.en: Because his dad was king. Another important influence in the Americas at this time was the French philosopher Montesquieu.
sentences.zh: 因为他的父亲是国王。当时美洲的另一个重要影响是法国哲学家孟德斯鸠。

sentences.en: Montesquieu argued that political power should be divided among different institutions.
sentences.zh: 孟德斯鸠认为政治权力应该在不同的机构之间分配。

sentences.en: By separating power, societies could reduce tyranny, or the risk of tyranny.
sentences.zh: 通过分离权力，社会可以减少暴政，或者减少暴政的风险。

sentences.en: These ideas would go on to later influence the American Constitution.​ By the summer of 1776, the conflict between Britain and the colonies had already started.
sentences.zh: 这些思想后来影响了美国宪法。到1776年夏天，英国与殖民地之间的冲突已经开始了。

sentences.en: It had already actually become violent. Fighting had started a year earlier in Massachusetts.
sentences.zh: 实际上它已经演变成暴力冲突。战斗在一年前的马萨诸塞州就已经打响。

sentences.en: In early 1776, a pamphlet called Common Sense was written by Thomas Paine.
sentences.zh: 1776年初，托马斯·潘恩写了一本名为《常识》的小册子。

sentences.en: The pamphlet argued that independence was necessary and logical for the American colonies.
sentences.zh: 这本小册子认为，独立对美洲殖民地来说是必要且合乎逻辑的。

sentences.en: It questioned why an island, Britain, thousands of miles away, should govern an entire continent.
sentences.zh: 它质疑为什么一个远在数千英里之外的岛屿——英国，应该统治整整一个大陆。

sentences.en: Why should Britain have the rights to govern North America?
sentences.zh: 为什么英国应该拥有统治北美的权利？

sentences.en: Then, in June 1776, delegates from the thirteen colonies met in Philadelphia to debate their future relationship with Britain.
sentences.zh: 然后，在1776年6月，来自十三个殖民地的代表在费城开会，讨论他们与英国未来的关系。

sentences.en: After weeks of discussion, they approved a document that is now one of the most famous political texts in history.
sentences.zh: 经过数周的讨论，他们批准了一份文件，该文件现在是历史上最著名的政治文本之一。

sentences.en: On July 4th, 1776, the Declaration of Independence was adopted.
sentences.zh: 1776年7月4日，《独立宣言》获得通过。

sentences.en: The Declaration explained why the colonies believed separation from Britain was justified.
sentences.zh: 《宣言》解释了为什么殖民地认为与英国分离是正当的。

sentences.en: It listed numerous grievances, like complaints, against King George III, and it argued that he had violated the rights of the colonists.
sentences.zh: 它列举了针对英王乔治三世的大量不满，即抱怨，并认为他侵犯了殖民地居民的权利。

sentences.en: It formally announced that the colonies were no longer British colonies.
sentences.zh: 它正式宣告这些殖民地不再是英国的殖民地。

sentences.en: They were now free and independent states.
sentences.zh: 它们现在是自由和独立的州。

sentences.en: The delegates who signed this document were effectively committing treason against the British Crown.
sentences.zh: 签署这份文件的代表实际上是在犯下针对英国王室的叛国罪。

sentences.en: They were betraying Britain because they were British subjects, right?
sentences.zh: 他们在背叛英国，因为他们本来就是英国臣民，对吧？

sentences.en: They weren’t Americans yet. They were British.
sentences.zh: 他们还不是美国人。他们是英国人。

sentences.en: If the revolution failed, they were going to be sent to prison or, more likely, executed, killed.
sentences.zh: 如果革命失败，他们将被送进监狱，或者更有可能被处决、杀死。

sentences.en: The declaration also introduced some really important ideas.
sentences.zh: 《宣言》还引入了一些非常重要的思想。

sentences.en: It argued that governments derive their powers from the consent of the governed.
sentences.zh: 它认为政府的权力源于被统治者的同意。

sentences.en: Legitimate governments rule because people agreed to be governed.
sentences.zh: 合法的政府进行统治是因为人民同意被统治。

sentences.en: That is an idea that was present in the Declaration of Independence.
sentences.zh: 那是《独立宣言》中呈现的一个想法。

sentences.en: But declaring independence and actually becoming independent are very different things.
sentences.zh: 但宣布独立和真正实现独立是两码事。

sentences.en: The new United States of America would need to go to war and defeat Britain to become independent.
sentences.zh: 崭新的美利坚合众国需要通过战争击败英国才能获得独立。

sentences.en: In 1776, Britain was probably the most powerful nation on Earth, and the newly declared United States was weak and divided.
sentences.zh: 在1776年，英国可能是地球上最强大的国家，而刚刚宣布独立的美国却软弱且分裂。

sentences.en: The Continental Army, which is the army of the United States, didn’t really have much food or clothes or weapons or money.
sentences.zh: 大陆军，也就是美国的军队，其实并没有多少食物、衣服、武器或金钱。

sentences.en: Their military units were part-time volunteers.
sentences.zh: 他们的军事单位是兼职志愿者。

sentences.en: They weren’t professional soldiers. So how did these American revolutionaries win?
sentences.zh: 他们不是职业军人。那么这些美国革命者是怎么赢的呢？

sentences.en: Well, Britain was going to have to fight a war across the Atlantic Ocean.
sentences.zh: 好吧，英国将不得不跨越大西洋打一场战争。

sentences.en: It was slow, expensive, and difficult to move things between North America and Britain, and also to move things across thirteen different colonies.
sentences.zh: 在北美和英国之间运送物资，以及在十三个不同的殖民地之间运送物资，速度慢、成本高且困难重重。

sentences.en: The colonies were also quite big, a lot of them massive, so controlling every single town and village was going to be impossible.
sentences.zh: 殖民地也相当大，其中许多规模庞大，因此控制每一个城镇和村庄将是不可能的。

sentences.en: Another reason, perhaps the biggest reason, was determination.
sentences.zh: 另一个原因，也许是最主要的原因，是决心。

sentences.en: The war was much more important for the people of the United States than it was for Britain.
sentences.zh: 这场战争对美国人民来说比对英国重要得多。

sentences.en: Of course, Britain did not want to lose the North American colonies.
sentences.zh: 当然，英国并不想失去北美殖民地。

sentences.en: Of course it didn’t. But if the war was getting too expensive, they’d give up.
sentences.zh: 当然不想。但如果战争变得太昂贵，他们就会放弃。

sentences.en: The USA was not going to give up if it got expensive.
sentences.zh: 如果代价高昂，美国是绝不会放弃的。

sentences.en: In 1777, American forces achieved a major victory at the Battle of Saratoga in New York.
sentences.zh: 1777年，美军在纽约的萨拉托加战役中取得了重大胜利。

sentences.en: The victory convinced France that the American revolutionaries had a chance of winning the war.
sentences.zh: 这场胜利让法国确信美国革命者有赢得战争的机会。

sentences.en: So in 1778, France joined in. France joined the side of the US.
sentences.zh: 所以在1778年，法国加入了。法国加入了美国这一边。

sentences.en: Spain and the Dutch also became involved in this broader conflict against Britain.
sentences.zh: 西班牙和荷兰也卷入了这场针对英国的更广泛冲突。

sentences.en: In 1781, the British General Charles Cornwallis was trapped between American and French forces on land, and a French fleet of naval boats at sea as well.
sentences.zh: 1781年，英国将军查尔斯·康沃利斯在陆地上被美国和法国军队夹击，在海上又被一支法国海军舰队包围。

sentences.en: He surrendered, and this was basically the point where Britain realized it could not win anymore.
sentences.zh: 他投降了，这基本上是英国意识到它再也无法取胜的关键节点。

sentences.en: Fighting continued, but in 1783, the Treaty of Paris formally recognized the independence of the United States.
sentences.zh: 战斗仍在继续，但在1783年，《巴黎条约》正式承认了美国的独立。

sentences.en: The American Revolution had been successful.
sentences.zh: 美国革命取得了成功。

sentences.en: The United States was now independent. But what kind of country was it going to be?
sentences.zh: 美国现在独立了。但它将会是一个什么样的国家呢？

sentences.en: Before the war, the thirteen colonies had been separate things.
sentences.zh: 战前，十三个殖民地一直是各自独立的存在。

sentences.en: They were not connected like the states of the US are today.
sentences.zh: 它们不像今天的美国各州那样紧密相连。

sentences.en: They were basically thirteen small countries.
sentences.zh: 它们基本上是十三个小国。

sentences.en: They came together, they worked together, to fight against the British.
sentences.zh: 它们走到一起，共同努力，对抗英国。

sentences.en: But after the war, what were they going to be?
sentences.zh: 但在战后，它们会变成什么样？

sentences.en: Were they going to unify into one strong country?
sentences.zh: 它们会统一成一个强大的国家吗？

sentences.en: The smaller colonies were worried that they would be dominated by the stronger and wealthier and larger colonies.
sentences.zh: 较小的殖民地担心它们会被更强、更富有、更大的殖民地主导。

sentences.en: But why would these small colonies give up their independence straight away?
sentences.zh: 但这些小殖民地为什么要直接放弃它们的独立呢？

sentences.en: And how do you create a government strong enough to function without creating another form of tyranny?
sentences.zh: 以及，你如何在不创造另一种形式的暴政的情况下，建立一个足够强大以运转的政府？

sentences.en: The first solution to this problem was the Articles of Confederation.
sentences.zh: 解决这个问题的第一个方案是《邦联条例》。

sentences.en: The Articles were adopted during the Revolutionary War and basically was the first constitution of the United States.
sentences.zh: 《条例》在独立战争期间通过，基本上是美国的宪法。

sentences.en: But the system the Articles introduced was nothing like the system the US has today.
sentences.zh: 但《条例》引入的系统与美国今天的系统完全不同。

sentences.en: For example, there was no president. Most of the political power was in the hands of the individual states.
sentences.zh: 例如，没有总统。大多数政治权力掌握在各个州手中。

sentences.en: The Articles did create some kind of national government, but the national government could only conduct foreign affairs and manage a few common issues.
sentences.zh: 《条例》确实建立了一种国家政府，但国家政府只能处理外交事务和管理一些共同事务。

sentences.en: Its power was really limited. This was the kind of government that the founders of the United States wanted.
sentences.zh: 它的权力真的很有限。这就是美国建立者们想要的政府。

sentences.en: They didn’t want a big, strong country. They wanted thirteen strong states.
sentences.zh: 他们不想要一个庞大、强大的国家。他们想要十三个强大的州。

sentences.en: Many people in the US believed that strong governments were dangerous.
sentences.zh: 美国许多人认为强大的政府是危险的。

sentences.en: The states wanted to protect their independence and their freedom.
sentences.zh: 各州希望保护它们的独立和自由。

sentences.en: People in Georgia did not want to be influenced by people in New York, and people in Massachusetts did not want to be influenced by people in Virginia.
sentences.zh: 佐治亚州的人不想受纽约州的人影响，马萨诸塞州的人不想受弗吉尼亚州的人影响。

sentences.en: The Articles created a loose confederation, a partnership of states, rather than a strong nation.
sentences.zh: 《条例》建立了一个松散的邦联，一个由各州组成的伙伴关系，而不是一个强大的国家。

sentences.en: As you can imagine, this causes problems.
sentences.zh: 正如你所想象的那样，这引发了问题。

sentences.en: The national government had no power. It couldn’t collect taxes, for example.
sentences.zh: 国家政府没有权力。例如，它不能征税。

sentences.en: But if the US needed to go to war, whether it was a war against Mexico or a war against Canada or a war against Britain again, or conflicts against Native Americans, it needed money.
sentences.zh: 但如果美国需要打仗，无论是对墨西哥的战争、对加拿大的战争、再次对英国的战争，还是对美洲原住民的冲突，它都需要钱。

sentences.en: If it needed money, it had to ask the states for money, because the states had the power.
sentences.zh: 如果它需要钱，它就得向各州要钱，因为各州拥有权力。

sentences.en: And the states didn’t always help. The states didn’t always give money to the national government.
sentences.zh: 而且各州并不总是帮忙。各州并不总是给国家政府钱。

sentences.en: The government struggled to pay its debts.
sentences.zh: 政府难以偿还债务。

sentences.en: It struggled to keep a military. There was no way it could regulate trade between states.
sentences.zh: 它难以维持军队。它根本无法监管州际贸易。

sentences.en: It couldn’t really do anything. The United States was acting like thirteen separate countries trying to cooperate.​ In 1787, delegates from twelve of the thirteen states (Rhode Island didn’t attend) went to Philadelphia again, and they met to discuss reforming the system.
sentences.zh: 它什么也做不了。美国就像十三个试图合作的独立国家。在1787年，来自十三州中十二个州的代表（罗德岛没有出席）再次前往费城，他们开会讨论改革这个系统。

sentences.en: Their original goal was to try and improve the Articles of Confederation, but instead they ended up making a completely new system of government.
sentences.zh: 他们最初的目标是试图改进《邦联条例》，但最终他们却制定了一个全新的政府系统。

sentences.en: The result was the United States Constitution.
sentences.zh: 结果就是《美国宪法》。

sentences.en: The Constitution tried to balance the need of the United States as a country with the needs of the individual states.
sentences.zh: 宪法试图平衡美国作为一个国家的需要与各个州的需要。

sentences.en: For example, all of the delegates discussing the Constitution wanted a stronger government, but they were also really suspicious of power.
sentences.zh: 例如，所有讨论宪法的代表都希望有一个更强大的政府，但他们也对权力高度猜忌。

sentences.en: The new government needed someone to carry out laws and lead the military and manage the government, so they created a role, the role of president.
sentences.zh: 新政府需要有人来执行法律、领导军队并管理政府，因此他们创造了一个职位，即总统的角色。

sentences.en: The president would be powerful but would not be a monarch.
sentences.zh: 总统将拥有权力，但不会成为君主。

sentences.en: The president would be elected. They would serve for a limited term, and they could be removed from office, and they had to obey a written constitution.
sentences.zh: 总统将通过选举产生。他们任期有限，可以被罢免，并且必须遵守成文宪法。

sentences.en: The Constitution also divided power between different institutions.
sentences.zh: 宪法还将权力分配给不同的机构。

sentences.en: Congress would make the laws. The president would enforce the laws.
sentences.zh: 国会制定法律。总统执行法律。

sentences.en: And the court would interpret the laws. Each branch of government could limit each other.
sentences.zh: 法院解释法律。政府的每个分支都可以互相制衡。

sentences.en: The Constitution also created a federal system.
sentences.zh: 宪法还创建了一个联邦系统。

sentences.en: Some powers belong to the national government, like the military and international relations, and other powers belong to the states.
sentences.zh: 一些权力属于国家政府，比如军队和国际关系，而其他权力则属于各州。

sentences.en: Eventually, the Constitution was ratified, was approved, and in 1789, the new government began operating.
sentences.zh: 最终，宪法得到了批准，并在1789年，新政府开始运作。

sentences.en: Later that year, George Washington became the first president of the United States.​
sentences.zh: 同年晚些时候，乔治·华盛顿成为美国第一任总统。

sentences.en: By 1789, the United States had won its independence from Britain and created a new constitutional system that was different from any other major nation.
sentences.zh: 到1789年，美国已经赢得了对英国的独立，并建立了一个不同于任何其他主要国家的崭新宪政系统。

sentences.en: But the United States in the late 18th century would seem very unfamiliar to us today.
sentences.zh: 但18世纪末的美国在我们今天看来会非常陌生。

sentences.en: The population was only around 4 million people, which is roughly the size of a city like Los Angeles today.
sentences.zh: 人口只有大约四00万人，大致相当于今天洛杉矶这样一座城市的规模。

sentences.en: Most North Americans lived in rural communities, and the United States was also much smaller geographically than it is today.
sentences.zh: 大多数北美洲人生活在农村社区，而且在地理上美国也比主要小得多。

sentences.en: It only occupied a narrow strip of land along the Atlantic coast.
sentences.zh: 它只占领了大西洋沿岸的一狭长地带。

sentences.en: Most of the land that is now part of the US was under the control of Native American nations, or Spain, or Britain, or France.
sentences.zh: 现在构成美国大部分的土地都受美洲原住民国家、西班牙、英国或法国的控制。

sentences.en: And American society contained a lot of contradictions.
sentences.zh: 而且美国社会包含了许多矛盾。

sentences.en: Slavery was legal, for example, despite all of that talk in the Constitution and the Declaration of Independence about liberty and equality.
sentences.zh: 例如，奴隶制是合法的，尽管宪法和独立宣言中有那么多关于自由和平等的言论。

sentences.en: Hundreds of thousands of African slaves lived and worked throughout the country, particularly in the South.
sentences.zh: 几十万名非洲奴隶在全国各地生活和工作，特别是在南方。

sentences.en: Women also possessed very few political rights, and voting was restricted to a relatively small portion of the population.
sentences.zh: 女性也几乎没有什么政治权利，投票权仅限于人口中相对较小的一部分。

sentences.en: But over time, the United States would gradually change.
sentences.zh: 但随着时间的推移，美国将逐渐发生改变。

sentences.en: It introduced the Bill of Rights and amendments to its Constitution.
sentences.zh: 它引入了《权利法案》及其宪法修正案。

sentences.en: It fought wars, including a big civil war, and expanded its territory.
sentences.zh: 它打过仗，包括一场大战——内战，并扩大了它的领土。

sentences.en: To me, the significance of 1776 and the Declaration of Independence is not necessarily that thirteen colonies broke away from Britain.
sentences.zh: 对我而言，1776年和《独立宣言》的意义不一定在于十三块殖民地脱离了英国。

sentences.en: Many colonies have done that. Britain used to control half the world.
sentences.zh: 许多殖民地都这样做过。英国过去控制了半个世界。

sentences.en: And many other colonies would gain independence.
sentences.zh: 而且许多其他殖民地也将获得独立。

sentences.en: And Britain had far more important colonies than North American ones.
sentences.zh: 并且英国拥有比北美殖民地重要得多的殖民地。

sentences.en: As much as people from the US think the US was the most important part of the British Empire, it wasn’t.
sentences.zh: 尽管美国人认为美国是英属帝国最重要的部分，但事实并非如此。

sentences.en: India was. India was far more important.
sentences.zh: 印度才是。印度要重要得多。

sentences.en: But I think what makes the American Revolution, and the Constitution, and the Declaration of Independence so important was the attempt to create a new political system.
sentences.zh: 但我认为让美国革命、宪法和独立宣言如此重要的原因，是试图创建一个新的政治系统。

sentences.en: Of course, the system they created had problems and flaws, and the United States has spent much of the past 250 years trying to fix its problems.
sentences.zh: 当然，他们创建的系统有问题和缺陷，美国在过去的二百五十年里花了很多时间试图修复其问题。

sentences.en: But creating a new system from nothing was a remarkable achievement, and so many countries around the world, so many of the countries that you guys are listening in, have political systems based on these events from 250 years ago.
sentences.zh: 但从零开始创建一个新的系统是一项非凡的成就，世界上如此多的国家，你们当中收听节目的许多国家，其政治系统都是基于250年前的这些事件。

sentences.en: But what do you think? What do you think about the US being 250 years old this year?
sentences.zh: 但你们怎么看？你们怎么看今年美国迎来250周年？

sentences.en: Have you ever visited the USA? Would you like to visit?
sentences.zh: 你们去过美国吗？你们想去吗？
